script: ATL +1 and a 51 total is a one-score game, so neither side is scripted into a blowout run-out or a pure pass chase. Bijan Robinson's 65 carries over weeks 3-5 (21.7 per game) stay in play, and Caleb Williams is not forced off the 23 Burden and 22 Odunze targets just because Chicago is a 1-point favorite.
who_goes_off: Bijan Robinson is the usage king: 425 rush yards on 65 carries (6.5 YPC) plus 11 targets and 53 receiving yards over weeks 3-5, against a CHI defense that has allowed 4.50 YPC and 12 runs of 10+. Drake London has the counting spike at 408 yards on 27 targets, but CHI's 13.61 YPA on 28 middle attempts is the hole a 3.8-aDOT Kyle Pitts (94 yards on 11 targets) actually fits.
weak_spot: CHI's real leak is the middle, 13.61 YPA on 28 attempts versus 6.67 left (51 att) and 8.27 right (51 att), so the matchup is LBs, nickel, and safeties, not outside corners, and the run front is soft at 4.50 YPC with 12 runs of 10+. ATL is the same shape in smaller size: 8.19 YPA on 27 middle attempts versus 6.42 left (92 att) and 5.44 right (91 att), with only 16 gains of 20+ on 222 attempts and a sturdier 4.04 YPC rush defense (8 runs of 10+).
injury_fallout: No injury absences are in the pre-kickoff data, so touches stay on the week 3-5 split: Swift 44 carries to Monangai's 40, Loveland 18 targets to Kmet's 5, and London 27 targets ahead of Pitts (11) and Dotson (10).
qb_vs_blitz: Caleb Williams is 0.20 EPA/dropback versus blitz (n=79) and -0.04 with no blitz, but ATL blitzes only 27%, so most of his dropbacks are the worse split. Michael Penix Jr. is 0.12 EPA versus blitz (n=59) and -0.27 with no blitz, and CHI's 38% blitz rate puts more than a third of his dropbacks into the split where he has actually been efficient.

picks.why: 65 carries and 425 yards over weeks 3-5 is 21.7 carries at 6.5 YPC, and ATL +1 does not take the ball away from him the way a blowout would. CHI has allowed 4.50 YPC and 12 runs of 10+ in five games, so 21 carries at 5.0 YPC is 105, clear of 95.5, even after regressing off the 6.5.

Odunze's 269 air yards on 22 targets (12.2 aDOT) is an outside vertical role, and that is ATL's best coverage at 5.44 YPA right (91 att) and 6.42 left (92 att), with only 16 passes of 20+ on 222 attempts. Williams is -0.04 EPA when not blitzed and ATL blitzes 27%, while Burden (23 targets) and Loveland (18) already crowd the 43.5.
